    • upload

    • uploadWithServiceAndTenantId

      public static void uploadWithServiceAndTenantId()
      Uploads an object while attaching an OperationContext that carries a service ID and tenant ID. The SDK stamps these identifiers onto the stored object's metadata (under the sdk-logging-service-id and sdk-logging-tenant-id keys) so that cloud audit logs (e.g. object access logs) can be traced back to the calling service and tenant.

      The correlationId is optional; when supplied it is echoed back on the UploadResponse so the caller can correlate this request across its own logs and traces. The serviceId and tenantId are supplied by the caller and are never auto-generated.

    • asyncUploadWithServiceAndTenantId

      public static void asyncUploadWithServiceAndTenantId()
      ASYNC counterpart of uploadWithServiceAndTenantId(). Threads a single OperationContext (serviceId / tenantId / correlationId) through the context-aware AsyncBucketClient APIs and blocks on each CompletableFuture so the demo runs sequentially and every SDK observability log line carries the same correlation_id / tenant_id / service_id MDC fields.

      Exercised APIs: upload(UploadRequest, byte[]), getMetadata(key, null, ctx), getTags(key, ctx), the multipart lifecycle (initiateMultipartUpload → uploadMultipartPart → listMultipartUpload → completeMultipartUpload), and both delete(...) overloads.

    • presignUploadWithTags

      public static void presignUploadWithTags()
      Presigns an upload URL that binds tags, including the reserved expiration-days tag, into the signature. The uploader must send every returned signed header verbatim, otherwise the upload is rejected. The expiration is measured from the time the URL is generated.

    • presignWithSessionCredentials

      public static void presignWithSessionCredentials() throws Exception
      Presigns upload and download URLs from a client that holds only short-lived session credentials, then uses them with a plain HTTP client, the way a caller without cloud credentials would.

      The session identity needs three things: permission to sign as itself (through the cloud's remote signing API when the credentials carry no private key), the signing API enabled for its project, and write/read access to the bucket. Signing does not check bucket access; the cloud checks it when the URL is used.

      Throws on any failure so main can report a clear pass or fail.

      Throws:
      Exception

    • multipartUploadWithServiceAndTenantId

      public static void multipartUploadWithServiceAndTenantId()
      Initiates a multipart upload while attaching an OperationContext that carries a service ID and tenant ID. The SDK stamps these identifiers onto the created object's metadata (under the sdk-logging-service-id and sdk-logging-tenant-id keys), mirroring the single-shot uploadWithServiceAndTenantId() path, so that cloud audit logs can be traced back to the calling service and tenant even for objects assembled from multiple parts.

      The correlationId is optional; when supplied it is also stamped onto the object metadata (under sdk-logging-correlation-id). The serviceId and tenantId are supplied by the caller and are never auto-generated.

    • setLifecycleExpirationTag

      public static void setLifecycleExpirationTag()
      Marks an object for lifecycle-based expiration using the reserved expiration-days tag.

      expiration-days is a reserved tag key. Setting it with a positive integer value marks the object as eligible for expiration, where the value is the number of days from the object's creation time after which it should expire. The SDK only classifies the object; it does not delete it. The actual deletion is performed by a bucket lifecycle rule that must be configured separately on the bucket. Once an object has been marked, the expiration can only be moved to a later time - lowering the value or removing the tag does not retract an expiration that was already scheduled.

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args)
      Walks through an upload/verify + download/verify + delete/verify cycle against the configured provider. Each step throws on failure so that the overall script exits non-zero if any assertion is violated, giving a clear pass/fail signal for the directory-operation code paths.

      Pass presign-session as the first argument to run only the session-credentials presign check (presignWithSessionCredentials()) instead.
